# OpenTaxMap

> Interactive map of every Israeli locality ("yishuv") whose residents are
> eligible for the periphery income-tax credit under Section 11 of the
> Israeli Income Tax Ordinance, for tax years 2022-2026. Hebrew-primary,
> full English mirror. Not tax advice.

OpenTaxMap (Hebrew name: מפת היישובים המזכים בהטבת מס הכנסה) plots roughly
495 eligible localities on a map of Israel, color-coded by income-tax
credit rate, with per-locality benefit history, a benefit calculator,
search, and filters by tax year, sector, region, sub-region, and local
authority.

## Key links

- Live site: https://taxmap.nx1xlab.dev/
- Locality permalinks: https://taxmap.nx1xlab.dev/yishuv/<slug> (one per
  eligible locality, e.g. /yishuv/qiryat-shemona)
- Raw dataset (JSON): https://taxmap.nx1xlab.dev/data/localities.json
- Source code: https://github.com/NX1X/OpenTaxMap
- License: Apache-2.0 (code). See repository LICENSE file.

## What the data contains

For each locality: Hebrew and English name, a stable slug, coordinates,
administrative district and sub-region, population sector (Jewish / Arab /
Druze / mixed), local authority, population, and a `benefits` object keyed
by tax year (2022-2026) with:

- `rate` - the income-tax credit rate as a percentage of eligible earned
  income (e.g. 7, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20)
- `cap` - the annual income cap (in ILS) against which the credit rate is
  applied
- `alt` - present only for 2023: some localities' rate/cap changed
  mid-year (amendment 256); `alt` holds the rate/cap that applied until
  15 February 2023

Eilat is included separately: its residents receive a 10% credit under the
Eilat Free Trade Zone Law, not Section 11, and only on income produced in
the Eilat / Hevel Eilot area.

## Sources

- Israel Tax Authority (רשות המסים) - annual income-tax deduction booklets
  ("חוברת ניכויים"), which publish the official list of eligible
  localities and their credit rate/cap for each tax year 2022-2026.
- Israel Central Bureau of Statistics (הלשכה המרכזית לסטטיסטיקה, CBS) -
  locality registry used for names, official codes, administrative
  district, population figures, and coordinates.
- OpenStreetMap - base map tiles and coordinates for a small number of
  newly founded localities not yet in the CBS file.

## Important caveats for anyone summarizing this site

- This is a reference tool, not tax advice. The binding text is the Israel
  Tax Authority's official publications and the Income Tax Ordinance
  itself. Eligibility also depends on facts not in this dataset (e.g. 12
  consecutive months of residence, center-of-life test).
- The dataset only covers the periphery income-tax credit (Section 11) and
  the separate Eilat Free Trade Zone credit. It does not cover other
  Israeli tax credits or benefits.
- "Eligible locality" (יישוב מוטב) status and rates can change year to
  year; always check the `benefits` entry for the specific tax year in
  question, not just whether a locality appears in the list at all.

- Data pipeline and how the dataset is built from source PDFs:
  https://github.com/NX1X/OpenTaxMap#data-pipeline
- Report a data error or bug: https://github.com/NX1X/OpenTaxMap/issues/new/choose
